newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA shares plunge after Jan report.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA shares plunge after Jan report.

text.p: Computer retailer CompUSA Inc shares dropped about 25 percent after reporting a disappointing 1.5 percent increase in December same-store sales.

Smith Barney vice president and retailing analyst Maureen McGrath said the market had been expecting a figure closer the three percent and the disappointing numbers are forcing analysts to cut CompUSA's fourth quarter earnings estimates.
Goldman Sachs had earlier cut its rating on CompUSA to "market perform" from "outperform."
CompUSA shares, down 4-1/4, are trading at 16-3/8.

McGrath, however, said CompUSA still retains a buy rating because of consolidation in the personal computer retailing as office superstores and consumer electronics retailers start to de-emphasize the personal computer business.
"This is a tough business to make money in," McGrath said.
McGrath also cited Tandy Corp's decision to close its Incredible Universe stores and several Computer City locations as a sign of consolidation.
In the future, upgrades of Intel Corp's Pentium chip should spur new computer sales, McGrath said.
